questions.question_text: Choose the correct comparison between $\frac{1}{7}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$.

options.why: This treats a larger denominator as a larger unit fraction.
Sevenths and halves are different-sized parts of the same whole.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct comparison between $\frac{1}{9}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$.

options.why: This treats the larger denominator as giving a larger unit fraction.
This treats equal numerators as making the fractions equal, although ninths and halves are different-sized parts.

questions.solution_text:
For the same whole, ninths are smaller parts than halves.
$\frac{1}{9}<\frac{1}{2}$

options.text: Each eighth of the same whole is smaller than each half.
Eight is greater than two, so the fraction is greater.
options.why: This transfers whole-number order directly to unit fractions.
No addition is involved in comparing these fractions.

questions.solution_text:
The same whole is split into more pieces.
Each eighth is smaller than each half.

questions.question_text:
A unit fraction is one of $3$, $4$, $5$, $6$, $8$ or $10$ equal parts of a whole.
How does it compare with $\frac{1}{2}$?

options.why: This reverses the unit-fraction denominator rule.
Only a denominator of two gives exactly one half.

questions.solution_text:
The whole is split into more than $2$ equal parts, so each part is smaller than a half.
It is less than $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.question_text: Which is the largest fraction in this list: $\frac{1}{31},\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{108},\frac{1}{450}$?

options.why: This overlooks one half; splitting the same whole into $31$ equal parts gives smaller parts than halves.
This treats a larger denominator than $2$ as giving a larger unit fraction, although more equal parts make each part smaller.
This chooses the largest denominator, which gives the smallest unit fraction in the list.

questions.solution_text:
For unit fractions of the same whole, the smaller denominator gives the larger value. Each other denominator is greater than $2$, so each other fraction is less than a half.
$\frac{1}{2}$ is the largest.

questions.question_text: A student writes $\frac{1}{200}>\frac{1}{2}$ because $200>2$. Which correction and explanation are correct?

options.text: $\frac{1}{200}<\frac{1}{2}$ because splitting the same whole into $200$ equal parts gives smaller parts than halves.

options.why: This repeats the student's mistake of transferring whole-number order directly to unit fractions.
This ignores the denominators; equal numerators do not make different-sized unit parts equal.

questions.solution_text:
The student has treated a larger denominator as a larger fraction. More equal parts of the same whole make each part smaller.
$\frac{1}{200}<\frac{1}{2}$
